Crush Utilization▼
0.0% (-1.5σ)
U.S. soybean crush at 0.0% of the 8.58M bu/day installed base in 2026-07, -1.51σ against 4 prior Juls (which averaged 0.0%). For scale, the industry's ~90.0%-of-nameplate working assumption is ~86.3% restated per calendar day (it assumes ~350 operating days), and crush is seasonally lightest in late spring/summer. Plants running softer than normal for the season. Crush VOLUME can still be near a record on a bigger plant base while utilization slips — it is utilization that says whether demand is actually pulling beans. ⚠️ Crush margin is in the top third of its range (100th pctile) while utilization is soft — margins say run hard and plants are not, which points at a physical constraint (new capacity still ramping, downtime, or bean availability) rather than economics.

CBOT soybeans (daily board) ⬇ CSV

Front-month soybean futures settle (¢/bu), daily. The price the whole signal board is actually a read ON — before this feed the newest price the tool could see was a monthly average published weeks late. Front-month continuous, so it carries a small step at each contract roll.

Loading chart…

Crush margin — board vs. Illinois cash ⬇ CSV

What a bushel is worth crushed, minus what it costs ($/bu). BOARD margin is computed from CBOT meal/oil/beans; ILLINOIS CASH uses observed AMS cash quotes. Yields follow the Gordon Denny workbook (meal 0.0221 t/bu, oil 11.71 lb/bu, hulls 0.0018 t/bu). Cash normally reads above board because observed Illinois cash meal and oil run over the synthetic board-plus-basis the workbook assumes. This is the cause side of crush demand — it leads plant utilization.

Loading chart…

Crush value share — oil vs. meal ⬇ CSV

Soybean oil's and meal's share of the product value from a crushed bushel (%), at the same workbook yields as the margin chart (oil 11.71 lb/bu, meal 0.0221 t/bu) — the industry "oil share". Meal share is the complement; hulls (~2% of value) are left out so the pair sums to 100. BOARD uses CBOT front-month oil/meal; ILLINOIS CASH uses AMS cash quotes. A rising oil share is the renewable-diesel pull showing up in the crush — it means meal is increasingly the byproduct, and plants run for oil even as meal backs up.

Loading chart…

Illinois soybean basis — all bids vs. processors ⬇ CSV

Cash bid minus futures (¢/bu), nearby month. The processor line is what crush plants themselves are bidding; when it runs above the all-Illinois average, crushers are paying up to pull beans in — a demand read no other series carries. Negative basis is normal.

Loading chart…

Soybean price received ⬇ CSV

Illinois daily cash ($/bu, AMS) against the monthly average price received — Illinois vs. U.S.

Soybean:corn price ratio ⬇ CSV

NASS Illinois prices received (monthly) and the CBOT nearby futures ratio (daily). Soybean price ÷ corn price — the relative-value read behind acreage decisions. Historically ~2.3–2.5 is the rough pivot between favoring beans and corn.

U.S. soybean stocks-to-use (WASDE) ⬇ CSV

Ending stocks as a share of total use — the tightness ratio that drives price. Roughly: below ~8% is tight (supportive), above ~15% is ample (a drag).

Soybean crop condition ⬇ CSV

In-season % rated good or excellent (USDA Crop Progress) — Illinois vs. U.S. Weather's fingerprint on this year's yield potential.

Crop vegetation index (satellite) ⬇ CSV

Weekly VegScape VCI (0–100) of crop vigor vs. the 2000-present range — Illinois + the core belt. MODIS-derived, ~4 days after each week closes, so it leads the NASS condition rating. Low = stress; high = a vigorous crop.

Loading chart…

Root-zone soil moisture (satellite) ⬇ CSV

Weekly Crop-CASMA / NASA SMAP volumetric soil moisture (m³/m³) — Illinois root-zone + surface, plus the core belt's root zone. The water available to the crop's roots: a cause-side stress read that leads the vegetation and condition reports.

Loading chart…

Illinois drought coverage ⬇ CSV

Share of Illinois land area in drought (D1+) and abnormally dry or worse (D0+), from the weekly U.S. Drought Monitor — a fast read on Corn Belt crop stress.

Loading chart…

Soybean exports (weekly) ⬇ CSV

Weekly export activity in metric tons — inspections (actual loadings) vs. net sales (forward bookings). An export-pace / China-demand read; net sales also stands in for the (currently offline) FAS report.

Loading chart…

Barge freight by river segment ⬇ CSV

Cost to move grain down-river ($/ton) on the river segments this deployment follows (state pack markets.barge.locations), plus the average of all reported segments — which mixes reaches priced very differently, so read the named segments. A driver of the Gulf export basis, and so of what Illinois elevators can bid.

Fund positioning (CFTC) ⬇ CSV

CBOT managed-money net position for soybeans, soybean meal and soybean oil (contracts) — how the funds are leaning. Extremes can unwind fast.
